title: Signal-Driven Threshold Composer + Explainability Timeline for Batch & Cache
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Design a composable UI that lets operators create signal-aware batch and cache threshold presets and then inspect a time-based explainability timeline that shows why a recommendation was generated, what upstream signals changed, and the simulated impact on latency and unit cost. This ticket covers low-fidelity exploration, a clickable prototype for usability testing, and a handoff package for engineering. The feature aims to reduce wrong configurations, speed up onboarding, and make rollback/rollout decisions auditable.
design_notes: Key constraints: must surface runtime signals (95th/99th latency, cache hit-rate, token distribution skew, request arrival bursts) without overwhelming the operator. Provide a compact composer that supports: (1) signal thresholds + weighting, (2) preset templates, (3) quick simulation with cost/latency delta, (4) one-click apply + canary rollout options. The explainability timeline should align with the Console's event stream and show candidate recommendations, accepted/rejected actions, and post-apply measured delta. Ensure compactness for users with many routes.
acceptance_criteria: Clickable prototype with composer + timeline validated in testing with 6 engineering/product participants
Design handoff (Figma frames + redlines) delivered and linked to ENG-2483
Prototype demonstrates simulation overlay with cost and latency delta estimates
Explainability timeline maps recommendations to concrete runtime signals and includes an exportable audit row
Composer supports saving at least three preset templates and a default safe preset
Accessibility: keyboard nav and color-contrast pass for key UI elements
tasks: Explore 3 layout patterns for composer (inline, modal, split-pane)
Define a compact signal taxonomy and visual encodings
Build prototype flows: create -> preview simulation -> apply canary
Run 6 moderated usability sessions and compile notes
Iterate on mockups based on research and PM feedback
Prepare developer-ready spec, tokens, and microcopy
